content_preview.title: OpenSSH 10.6p2 Fixes a Password Authentication Bypass Affecting musl-Based Linux Systems With PAM Disabled, Including Alpine Linux
content_preview.summary: OpenSSH's 10.6p2 release, dated 2026-11-05, works around a password bypass on musl-based Linux without PAM; BleepingComputer names Alpine Linux among affected systems.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The OpenSSH project published Portable OpenSSH 10.6p2 on 2026-11-05, according to its [release notes](https://www.openssh.org/releasenotes.html). The notes say the release "contains a critical security workaround that affects Linux systems that use the musl libc and PAM disabled." The release follows OpenSSH 10.6, which the Herald [previously reported](/article/2026-10/07-openssh-106-disables-lz77-compression-over-a-plaintext-recovery-attack-enables-hybrid-post-quantum-signatures-an...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear News structure (Overview, release notes, mechanism per BleepingComputer, mitigation, AI-tools context, other changes, What We Don't Know). 761 words, within News range 400-1200. Title is 130 characters (under 150). Attribution is consistently explicit: the affected-distribution list (Alpine Linux, OpenWrt, Buildroot, Yocto), the 2016 origin, the exploitation conditions and the 17,600-test figure are all presented as BleepingComputer's reporting, not as the Herald's own statements.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all four snapshots from sources/2026-11/ (gunzip, tag-stripped text) and cross-checked the raw upstream commit patch (github .patch), the live openssh.org notes and the live BleepingComputer page via curl with browser User-Agent. (0) source-0 openssh.org release notes: 10.6p2 dated 2026-11-05; 'This release contains a critical security workaround that affects Linux systems that use the musl libc and PAM disabled' verbatim; security entry quoted verbatim ('We consider the root cause of this bug to be outside sshd, but it is exploitable via sshd and can be avoided there'); credit 'Özgün Kültekin of Wakefield (wakefield.co)' verbatim; no CVE in the 10.6p2 section; AI-reports paragraph and 'more frequent releases' sentence verbatim (the sentence sits in the release intro, not tied to this bug, as the article says); bugfixes ssh-mldsa44-ed25519 as CA signature algorithm and '<1 second CPU spin if ChannelTimeout' confirmed. No Anthropic involvement in the 10.6p2 section (Anthropic/Claude mentions in the page belong to older releases, unrelated). (1) source-1 BleepingComputer (Lawrence Abrams, Nov 5 2026; Archive.org fallback snapshot, status 200 live also checked): '*sshole' name; musl list 'including Alpine Linux, OpenWrt, Buildroot, and Yocto' attributed to BleepingComputer; 'since 2016' attributed to Kultekin; 2016 patch for CVE-2016-6210 username enumeration; crypt() returns * incl. 256-byte limit; five exploitation conditions; PAM 'as it is by default in Alpine Linux's openssh-server package'; 'does not allow attackers to bypass passwords on accounts with valid password hashes'; glibc 'Debian, Ubuntu, and Fedora' not vulnerable; AWS/Azure alpine account with passwordless doas; 17,600 tests by AI agents; fixed in 10.6p2; PasswordAuthentication no workaround. All match. Minor note: the first quote in the article ('...accounts that are configured to block password authentication, simply by entering an oversized password') is verbatim from BleepingComputer's page metadata (meta description/structured data in the live page head) while the visible body reads 'accounts configured to block password authentication simply by entering...'; same wording otherwise, no substantive difference, no correction needed. (2) source-2 oss-security post by Jan Schaumann (Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:14:35 -0500): 'checking for MIN_PASSWORD_HASH_LEN instead of using musl crypt(3)'s default "*"' verbatim; 'at the obvious cost of not being able to do password auth' verbatim; Alpine 'called out'; workaround matches. The post links sshhole.com (not allowlisted, correctly omitted by the writer). (3) source-3 GitHub commit 4353fdc (confirmed via raw .patch): author Damien Miller, Date Thu, 5 Nov 2026 08:18:18 +1100, subject 'avoid password authn bypass'; message quote verbatim; '#define MIN_PASSWORD_HASH_LEN 4' and 'strlen(pw_password) >= MIN_PASSWORD_HASH_LEN' added to the comparison in auth-passwd.c, confirmed. Absences confirmed: no CVE id for this bypass in sources 0, 2, 3 (grep zero) and source 1 mentions only CVE-2016-6210 (the historical enumeration bug, correctly not conflated); no source reports exploitation in the wild (BleepingComputer only gives log-check advice 'could indicate that the vulnerability was exploited'); no source lists distro package versions (BleepingComputer gives only 'apk upgrade openssh'). Pattern scan: suspicious_patterns null for all four. Independent-source recount: BleepingComputer and the oss-security post are independent of the OpenSSH project; openssh.org and the GitHub commit are first-party. 2 independent, 2 first-party (News, so no Analysis threshold applies).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All dates, versions, names, numbers, quotes and code details trace to the cited sources. Prior Herald piece linked (/article/2026-10/07-openssh-106-...) exists, covers OpenSSH 10.6 (LZ77 disable, hybrid PQ signatures, scp -R deprecation) and is described accurately; the 'follows OpenSSH 10.6' phrasing is consistent with the notes' 'Changes since OpenSSH 10.6p1'. Nothing in the body asserts an unsourced claim. 'All of the following' (five exploitation conditions) matches BleepingComputer's list exactly. Absolute dates only; no relative dates. Researcher's 'flaw existed since 2016' and '17,600 tests' each rest on BleepingComputer alone and are attributed as such. Minor nuance not in the article: the oss-security post says passwords >257 characters trigger it while BleepingComputer cites a 256-byte limit; the article states neither threshold, so no conflict.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and attributive. The release notes' own 'critical' wording is quoted, not adopted. No sensationalism, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: New topic: no existing Herald article covers the sshole/musl bypass or 10.6p2 (grep of articles for sshole/OpenSSH 10.6p2 found only the prior 10.6 article, which is linked). Not a duplicate.
recommendations: Optional future refinement: mention that the oss-security post gives the trigger length as more than 257 characters while BleepingComputer cites a 256-byte limit, if the thresholds are ever discussed.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-attributed News coverage of a security fix with every quote and figure verified against raw source text; Anthropic is not involved in the sources, so no contributor-model clarification is needed. Verdict APPROVE. Featured candidacy: 2 - notable security fix for a widely deployed daemon, with a concrete exposure (Alpine official cloud images) relevant to a broad sysadmin audience, but not industry-changing
